question: What is MCP in the context of Claude Code?

options.text: A memory management system for the context window
options.explanation: MCP stands for Model Context Protocol and is responsible for external integrations, not memory management

options.text: A standard protocol for connecting external tools to an agent
options.explanation: Model Context Protocol is the standard through which Claude Code can interact with any external service: GitHub, databases, Figma, etc.

options.text: The format of Claude Code's configuration files
options.explanation: MCP is a protocol for interacting with external tools, not a configuration file format

options.text: An encryption mechanism for data between the agent and the server
options.explanation: MCP is an integration protocol, not an encryption mechanism. Security is handled by other means

question: Which MCP transport is used in most cases for local development?

options.text: HTTP -- a remote URL
options.explanation: HTTP is used for hosted/corporate servers, not for local development

options.text: stdio -- a local process via stdin/stdout
options.explanation: stdio is the simplest and most common transport. Claude Code launches the MCP server as a child process and communicates via stdin/stdout

options.text: WebSocket -- a bidirectional stream
options.explanation: WebSocket (type: ws) is a full-fledged MCP transport, but a niche one: it's needed when the server pushes events itself. For local development this is unnecessary complexity

options.text: SSE -- Server-Sent Events
options.explanation: SSE is a remote transport, and it's also marked as deprecated. The documentation recommends using HTTP instead

question: What is the correct way to pass a GitHub token in an MCP server configuration?

options.text: Pass it as a command-line argument: "args": ["--token", "ghp_abc123"]
options.explanation: Hardcoding the token in arguments has the same leak problem. Use env with environment variables

options.text: Write it in a separate .mcp-secrets.json file
options.explanation: No such file exists in MCP configuration. Use environment variables with $

options.text: Hardcode it directly in .mcp.json: "GITHUB_TOKEN": "ghp_abc123"
options.explanation: A hardcoded token will leak when .mcp.json is committed to git. Always use environment variables

options.text: Via an environment variable: "GITHUB_TOKEN": "$GITHUB_TOKEN"
options.explanation: Values with $ are substituted from environment variables. The token is stored locally, not in the config

question: Which file is responsible for MCP server configuration at the project level?

options.text: package.json in the mcp section
options.explanation: MCP servers are configured in .mcp.json, not in package.json

options.text: .mcp.json in the project root
options.explanation: The project MCP configuration is stored in .mcp.json in the repository root and is usually committed, so the whole team gets the same set of servers

options.text: .claude/settings.json
options.explanation: settings.json contains Claude Code settings (hooks, permissions), not MCP server configuration

options.text: ~/.claude/.mcp.json in the home directory
options.explanation: This path doesn't exist -- Claude Code doesn't read it. User-level servers are stored in ~/.claude.json under the mcpServers key

question: The GITHUB_TOKEN variable is set like this: GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_abc123 (without export). What happens when the MCP server starts?

options.text: The server will start, but the token will be an empty string
options.explanation: Technically true (the token will be empty), but the result is an authentication error, so the first option describes the consequences more accurately

options.text: Claude Code will automatically add export
options.explanation: Claude Code doesn't modify the user's environment variables. You need to use export explicitly

options.text: Everything will work fine
options.explanation: Without export, the variable isn't visible to child processes. The MCP server will get an empty value

options.text: The MCP server won't see the variable -- authentication error
options.explanation: Without export, the variable is only available in the current shell. The MCP server runs as a child process and won't inherit it

question: The project and global configuration both contain an MCP server named 'db'. What happens?

options.text: Both servers will start in parallel
options.explanation: The server name is a unique identifier. On a collision, the project configuration overrides the global one

options.text: The project configuration will completely override the global one for this server
options.explanation: A same-named server in the project configuration takes priority and completely replaces the global setting

options.text: The global configuration takes priority
options.explanation: The opposite is true: the project (more specific) configuration overrides the global one

options.text: There will be a configuration conflict error
options.explanation: There won't be a conflict -- the project configuration simply overrides the global one for the same-named server

question: You've connected 15 MCP servers at once. What problem might arise?

options.text: The MCP servers will conflict with each other
options.explanation: Servers are isolated from each other. The problem isn't conflicts, but overloading Claude's context

options.text: Claude sees too many tools, spends context on their descriptions, and may pick the wrong tool
options.explanation: Each MCP server adds tools to the context. 200+ tools slow things down, consume context window space, and increase the chance of choosing the wrong tool

options.text: There won't be a problem -- the more servers, the better
options.explanation: More servers = more tools in the context = slower selection + context window consumption. Only connect what you need

options.text: There's a limit -- 10 MCP servers, 15 won't start
options.explanation: There's no hard limit, but a large number of servers degrades quality of work due to context overload

question: What is Managed MCP used for in a corporate environment?

options.text: To automatically install all MCP servers on developers' machines
options.explanation: Managed MCP manages access, not installation. Servers still need to be installed on each machine

options.text: To control, via allowlist/denylist, which MCP servers developers may connect
options.explanation: Managed MCP lets administrators control the available servers through allow/deny lists and centralized configuration

options.text: To encrypt data between Claude Code and MCP servers
options.explanation: Managed MCP is about access management (which servers are allowed), not data encryption

options.text: To monitor MCP server performance
options.explanation: Managed MCP is an access-control mechanism (allowlist/denylist), not monitoring

question: What three types of resources can an MCP server provide?

options.text: Read, Write, Execute
options.explanation: These are operation abstractions, not MCP resource types. The three types are: tools, resources, and prompts

options.text: Tools (functions), Resources (data), Prompts (templates)
options.explanation: An MCP server provides tools to call, resources to read, and prompt templates

options.text: Commands, Files, Logs
options.explanation: The MCP protocol defines three types: tools, resources, and prompts -- these are the standard categories

options.text: Input, Output, Context
options.explanation: These are not MCP resource types. The protocol defines tools, resources, and prompts

question: You're building an MCP server for an internal company system. Which transport should you choose for shared access without installing it on every machine?

options.text: stdio -- a local process
options.explanation: stdio requires installing a package on every machine. For shared access, HTTP is better

options.text: HTTP -- a remote server accessible via URL
options.explanation: The HTTP transport lets you deploy the MCP server centrally. Developers connect via URL without a local install

options.text: It's impossible -- MCP only works locally
options.explanation: MCP supports remote transports: HTTP, WebSocket, and the deprecated SSE -- they don't require a local install

options.text: SSE -- for any corporate scenario
options.explanation: SSE is marked as deprecated, and the documentation recommends HTTP instead. For shared access, HTTP is the right choice

question: What happens if the Python package for the MCP server isn't installed?

options.text: Claude Code will fail to start
options.explanation: Claude Code won't crash, but the MCP server won't start -- its tools simply won't be available

options.text: The server will start, but with limited functionality
options.explanation: Without the installed package, the process won't start at all -- ModuleNotFoundError

options.text: Claude Code will automatically install the package via pip
options.explanation: Claude Code doesn't automatically install Python packages. This needs to be done manually before use

options.text: Claude Code won't see this server's tools -- it simply won't start
options.explanation: Unlike npx servers (which download automatically), Python servers must be installed manually. Without installation, the process won't start

question: Which MCP server lets Claude Code get up-to-date library documentation?

options.text: Context7
options.explanation: The Context7 MCP server provides access to up-to-date documentation and code examples for any library

options.text: There's no such server -- Claude uses its training data
options.explanation: The Context7 MCP server is specifically designed to provide up-to-date library documentation

options.text: Notion
options.explanation: The Notion MCP server works with your Notion documents, not with external library documentation

options.text: GitHub
options.explanation: The GitHub MCP server works with PRs, issues, and repositories, not with library documentation
